successors.name: Mycenaean Greece
successors.text: Crete: 'a Mycenaean elite clearly ruling Knossos from around 1450 BC'

ledger.x: c. 1900 BCE: the first palaces rise on Crete. Knossos page: 'The first palace was built around 1900 BC'; Minoan page: the first palaces date to MM IB (c. 1925-1875 BC). The page gives the palace sites, not a boundary; the whole island is drawn.

c. 1450 BCE: the palaces burn and a Mycenaean elite rules Knossos; Crete passes to Mycenaean Greece. Knossos page: 'The palace was partially destroyed around 1450 BC, during a wider period of disruption affecting many Minoan sites' and 'After about 1450 BC, Knossos became an important Mycenaean administrative centre'.…

certainty.note: No borders exist: the shape is the island of Crete, drawn as a whole, while 'it is unclear whether there was ever a unified Minoan state'.
